samples.summary: Unrelated scope creep: a frontend visual-harness font-waiting rewrite is bundled into a CLI error-envelope change
samples.evidence: The diff's stated subject is the CLI upstream-error forwarding helpers (`forwardUpstreamError` / `upstreamErrorJson` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts) applied across docs/notes/slides/files. The hunk in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs is a wholly separate concern: it expands VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES with Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, adds a VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS matrix, adds a catch-all `status !== 'loading'` poll, and relocates `waitForFontsReady(page)` from before the harness-root wait to after the section-ready wait (capturePass). It shares no module, no test, and no acceptance criterion with the CLI work, and it materially changes when screenshots are taken in the visual-baseline lane (a change that can shift/invalidate the ~220 pinned baselines described in docs/design/harness-engineering.md). It should be its own change so it can be reviewed and baselined independently.

samples.summary: The two new helpers emit different `error.code` for the identical failure condition, splitting the agent-facing contract
samples.evidence: For the same input — a non-envelope upstream failure — `forwardUpstreamError` throws `HTTP <status>`, which `outputError` flattens to `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` (formatter.ts:46,109), while `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` (formatter.ts:129). The new test file asserts both divergent shapes (test/upstream-error.test.ts:191 expects `code: 'ERROR'` for `docs content`; :462 expects `code: 'HTTP_ERROR'` for `docs import`). The whole justification in the doc comments is that agents branch on `code`; making the code depend on which command family happened to fail is exactly the ambiguity the change set out to remove. One helper (or one code) would satisfy the same goal.

samples.summary: The new envelope-forwarding helper is not applied to the sheets/api-keys/files/metadata command sites, leaving a documented error-matrix row unmet
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §10 documents `sheets.cells.get` on a doc-typed document as exit 1 with code `TYPE_MISMATCH` (line 1029), symmetric with the `docs.content` row this change fixes. But every sheets/cells/tabs/api-keys/files/metadata site still does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\`HTTP ${res.status}\`)` (cells.ts:25,65,91,143; tabs.ts:16,49,75; api-keys.ts:18,32,46; files.ts:86,106,124,142; docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40-117; slides.ts:45-122), so the backend's `TYPE_MISMATCH` envelope is discarded and the agent sees `{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 4xx"}`. The change introduces exactly the helper needed and applies it to only six of the sites, so the asymmetry documented in cli.md remains.

samples.summary: New non-envelope mapping contradicts the documented exit-code/code matrix for 401/403 and 5xx
samples.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §10 specifies backend 401/403 → exit 2, code `UNAUTHORIZED`, and backend 5xx/network → exit 2, code `SYSTEM`. Both new helpers collapse every non-envelope failure to exit 1 with `ERROR`/`HTTP_ERROR` and no status-based branch, and the new tests cement that (`status: 502` → `HTTP_ERROR`, test/upstream-error.test.ts:210). This is largely pre-existing behaviour, but the change makes formatter.ts the single canonical place where upstream status is turned into a code, which is precisely where the documented matrix would be honoured or the doc updated.

samples.summary: `output/formatter.ts`'s role changed but its design-doc description was not updated, and `HTTP_ERROR` is absent from the error matrix
samples.evidence: cli.md §7 describes `output/formatter.ts` as "Format dispatcher (json | table | csv | yaml)"; it now also owns upstream-error envelope policy for every content/export/import path. The `HTTP_ERROR` code the helpers now emit appears in packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84 and slides-import-pptx.md:72 but in neither cli.md §10's Error Matrix nor packages/cli/README.md:116-120 (which states everything non-typed "reports `\"ERROR\"`"). Per CONTRIBUTING the canonical subsystem doc should absorb this rather than the codes living only in skill files.
searchedFor: grep HTTP_ERROR across packages/cli and docs/design

samples.summary: A second local envelope builder (`errorJson`) now sits beside the shared helper in the same file
samples.evidence: upload.ts imports `upstreamErrorJson` (line 4) yet keeps its own private `errorJson(code, message)` producing the same `{error:{code,message}}` shape (line 225-227), used for FILE_TOO_LARGE/FILE_READ_FAILED. If the goal is one canonical envelope constructor in output/formatter.ts, the local duplicate should fold into it (or the shared helper should expose the primitive) rather than two builders coexisting.

finding.summary: Unrelated scope creep: a frontend visual-harness font-waiting rewrite is bundled into a CLI error-envelope change
finding.evidence: The diff's stated subject is the CLI upstream-error forwarding helpers (`forwardUpstreamError` / `upstreamErrorJson` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts) applied across docs/notes/slides/files. The hunk in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs is a wholly separate concern: it expands VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES with Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, adds a VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS matrix, adds a catch-all `status !== 'loading'` poll, and relocates `waitForFontsReady(page)` from before the harness-root wait to after the section-ready wait (capturePass). It shares no module, no test, and no acceptance criterion with the CLI work, and it materially changes when screenshots are taken in the visual-baseline lane (a change that can shift/invalidate the ~220 pinned baselines described in docs/design/harness-engineering.md). It should be its own change so it can be reviewed and baselined independently.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element exists as described. verify-visual-browser.mjs:346-356 adds Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono to VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES; :362 adds the VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS [400,500,600,700] matrix; :394-398 adds the catch-all `face.status !== "loading"` poll; and :422-434 places waitForFontsReady after the harness-root and section-ready waits (the in-file comment and the task doc at 20260811-visual-inter-font-race-todo.md:38-47 confirm this is a relocation from before those waits). The originating CLI task doc (20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:42-58) scopes outcome/acceptance strictly to packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts and the six forwarding sites; no acceptance criterion or non-goal covers the frontend visual harness. The visual work is tracked by its own separate task doc that describes it as a pre-existing harness race unrelated to the branch, and it touches the pinned-baseline capture lane described in docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2403. Unrequested scope creep is explicitly in the design-fit lane and rated major, so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.

finding.summary: The two new helpers emit different `error.code` for the identical failure condition, splitting the agent-facing contract
finding.evidence: For the same input — a non-envelope upstream failure — `forwardUpstreamError` throws `HTTP <status>`, which `outputError` flattens to `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` (formatter.ts:46,109), while `upstreamErrorJson` returns `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` (formatter.ts:129). The new test file asserts both divergent shapes (test/upstream-error.test.ts:191 expects `code: 'ERROR'` for `docs content`; :462 expects `code: 'HTTP_ERROR'` for `docs import`). The whole justification in the doc comments is that agents branch on `code`; making the code depend on which command family happened to fail is exactly the ambiguity the change set out to remove. One helper (or one code) would satisfy the same goal.

verdict.reason: The two divergent codes exist exactly as quoted (formatter.ts:46,109 -> 'ERROR'; formatter.ts:129 -> 'HTTP_ERROR'), but the divergence is what the originating issue's acceptance criteria explicitly require: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:44-47 mandates `{"error":{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` on the content/export paths AND `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 404"}}` on the import/upload/download paths. Both codes are pre-existing published contract, not invented by this change: packages/cli/README.md:116-120 says everything untyped reports "ERROR", while packages/cli/skills/docs-import-docx.md:84 and skills/slides-import-pptx.md:72 already promise HTTP_ERROR for the import paths (and test/files-upload.test.ts:31,223 shows HTTP_ERROR was the emitted code there before this change). Collapsing to one code would violate those documented skill files and the stated criterion. The one criterion about sharing is met: both helpers route through the single isErrorEnvelope guard (formatter.ts:76-85, called at :104 and :127), satisfying todo.md:50-51. Hence the finding is a taste preference ("one helper or one code would be nicer") that contradicts the spec rather than an unmet acceptance criterion, duplicated module, or Non-Goal breach — minor at most under the design-fit rubric, not blocking.

finding.summary: The new envelope-forwarding helper is not applied to the sheets/api-keys/files/metadata command sites, leaving a documented error-matrix row unmet
finding.evidence: docs/design/cli.md §10 documents `sheets.cells.get` on a doc-typed document as exit 1 with code `TYPE_MISMATCH` (line 1029), symmetric with the `docs.content` row this change fixes. But every sheets/cells/tabs/api-keys/files/metadata site still does `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(\`HTTP ${res.status}\`)` (cells.ts:25,65,91,143; tabs.ts:16,49,75; api-keys.ts:18,32,46; files.ts:86,106,124,142; docs.ts:80,107,121,139,157; notes.ts:40-117; slides.ts:45-122), so the backend's `TYPE_MISMATCH` envelope is discarded and the agent sees `{"code":"ERROR","message":"HTTP 4xx"}`. The change introduces exactly the helper needed and applies it to only six of the sites, so the asymmetry documented in cli.md remains.

verdict.reason: The code observation is accurate (cells/tabs/api-keys/files still do `if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`)`), but it is not a design-fit violation of this change. (1) The originating issue, docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md, names exactly the six sites the change fixes (lines 13-18) and its Non-goals section (lines 53-58) explicitly excludes "`sheets cells` / `sheets export`, which flatten or cast an upstream envelope rather than forwarding it verbatim — a different defect, left for a follow-up", plus "Any change to the backend's error bodies." Under this lens, exceeding a Non-goal is a violation; declining to do work the issue explicitly deferred is not. Its acceptance criteria are met: criterion 3 requires "Every CLI path that PRINTS an upstream body shares one guard (`isErrorEnvelope`)", and the cells/tabs/api-keys/files sites print nothing upstream — they throw into outputError. (2) The finding's stated mechanism is also factually wrong: no TYPE_MISMATCH envelope is discarded on the cells path, because the backend never emits one there. TYPE_MISMATCH_BODY exists only in docs-content.controller.ts:42-44 (thrown at :88); cells.controller.ts throws only NotFoundException (:58,:91,:117,:142,:161) and tabs.controller.ts throws a plain BadRequestException with a string message (:43-47). Both are framework-shaped bodies that isErrorEnvelope (formatter.ts:76-85) deliberately rejects, so applying forwardUpstreamError to those sites would produce byte-identical output (`HTTP 4xx`). The cli.md:1029 error-matrix row is therefore an unimplemented backend behavior, pre-existing and explicitly out of this issue's scope, not an asymmetry this CLI change could have closed.
